record.title: verify-receipt aborts with a Rust panic (exit 101, no verdict) on a receipt whose hex fields or attestation key are not ASCII
record.description: `zanary-report verify-receipt` exists so a stranger can check a receipt somebody else supplied: main.rs:104-106 reads the path from argv and deserializes it into `zanary_observation::Receipt`, whose `signer`, `signature` and `attestation.{format,receipt_key,wallet_ak,signature}` fields are arbitrary UTF-8 `String`s (crates/observation/src/lib.rs:115-141), and receipt.rs then slices those strings by BYTE offset - `hex_decode` (receipt.rs:352-363, reached from receipt.rs:65,72,157,165) and the display helper `short` (receipt.rs:188-194, reached from main.rs:188-189 and receipt.rs:145-146,151-154). `hex_decode` only checks that the byte length is even before `u8::from_str_radix(&hex[i..i + 2], 16)`, and `short` only checks `hex.len() > 20` before `&hex[..8]` / `&hex[hex.len() - 8..]` on the same line; slicing a `&str` panics when the index falls inside a multi-byte character. A receipt whose `signer` is `a\u20ac` (4 bytes, even) aborts the verifier before any verdict line is printed; a receipt whose signed fields are perfectly valid and which carries an `attestation` object whose `receipt_key` is not ASCII passes `signature : VALID` and both `claim ok` lines and then panics inside `short()` on the no-`--fvk` branch (main.rs:184-190) - reachable because the attestation is not part of the signed bytes, as the crate's own test asserts (receipt.rs:487-504) and as this verifier re-established by attaching the attestation after signing and still seeing `signature : VALID`. The tool's contract is an exit code a caller or workflow reads (0 verified, 1 FAIL, 2 input error; main.rs:49-55, 135-137, 199-200); a panic is none of those, so for that artifact the caller gets no verdict at all. Both variants were independently reproduced by this verifier in the sandbox from fixtures generated by the target's own signing code (check-cli-repro.txt, check-unit-probe.txt).
record.root_cause: Byte-offset slicing of caller-controlled strings guarded only by a byte length: `hex_decode` slices `&hex[i..i + 2]` (receipt.rs:359) after `hex.len().is_multiple_of(2)` (receipt.rs:353) and `short` slices `&hex[..8]` and `&hex[hex.len() - 8..]` (receipt.rs:190) after `hex.len() > 20` (receipt.rs:189). Neither calls `is_char_boundary` nor rejects non-ASCII, so any multi-byte UTF-8 character straddling an index panics with "end byte index N is not a char boundary".
record.intended_behavior: Malformed receipt fields are reported, not fatal: the existing error paths return `hex string has an odd length`, `the signer key is N bytes, expected 32` and `the signer key is not a valid Orchard spend-authorizing key`, the CLI prints `signature : INVALID` / `claim : INVALID` and exits 1, and `--fvk` mismatches exit 1 (main.rs:120-138, 174-181; receipt.rs:352-363; docs/FLOW-RUNNER-NOTES.md:343-355 documents the same malformed-receipt rows as exit 1). Every parseable receipt file should produce a verdict with exit 0 (pass), 1 (FAIL) or 2 (input error, e.g. an undecodable UFVK) - never a process abort; the ASCII controls in this verification exit 0 on the same binaries.

trace.description: reads the caller-given receipt path and deserializes the file as zanary_observation::Receipt (104-106); signer/signature/attestation fields are unvalidated Strings
u8::from_str_radix(&hex[i..i + 2], 16) slices the caller-supplied signer/signature/attestation-key string by byte index after only an even-length check -> panic (observed at 359:36)
with no --fvk, a receipt that passed both checks and carries an attestation has its unvalidated receipt_key/wallet_ak echoed through short() (184-190)
&hex[..8] and &hex[hex.len() - 8..] on the same line slice the caller-supplied key by byte index after only a length check -> panic (observed at 190:30)

evidence.description: hex_decode's only guard on the caller-supplied input before slicing is `hex.len().is_multiple_of(2)`
the byte-offset slice `&hex[i..i + 2]` that panics: "end byte index 2 is not a char boundary; it is inside '\u20ac' (bytes 1..4 of string)"

short()'s `&hex[..8]` and `&hex[hex.len() - 8..]` slices - both are on this line (line 191 is `} else {`) - that panic: "end byte index 8 is not a char boundary; it is inside '\u20ac' (bytes 7..10 of string)"
first sink on the verdict path: hex_decode(signer_hex), reached before any other check in verify_signature; three more call sites at receipt.rs:72, 157, 165
the receipt is read from a caller-given path (main.rs:104) and parsed with serde_json (105-106), so every field is attacker-chosen text
signer: Option<String> - no charset validation (signature at :118, attestation at :124, attestation.receipt_key/wallet_ak at :136/:138, attestation.signature at :140)

the crate's own test `the_attestation_is_not_part_of_the_receipt_signature` (487-504) proves the attestation is outside the signed bytes, so one can be attached to an already-signed receipt - re-established locally: my fixture was signed before the attestation was attached and still printed `signature : VALID`
the no---fvk branch (184-190) that echoes an unvalidated attestation through short(), i.e. the second sink is reached with only a validly signed receipt
verify_attestation's mismatch messages call short() on the caller-supplied receipt_key and signer (145-146, 151-154), the same unchecked slice under --fvk
the exit-code contract: Ok(code) -> exit(code), Err -> exit(2) (49-55), FAIL -> Ok(1) (135-137), success -> Ok(0) (199-200); a Rust panic produces 101 instead, outside the contract

conditions.description: A receipt file with a multi-byte UTF-8 character at a non-char-boundary byte index in `signer` (variant A; no valid signature required - the panic precedes every check, and "a\u20ac" is 4 bytes so it passes the even-length guard), or in `signature`/`attestation.wallet_ak`/`attestation.signature`; variant B (the short() sink) additionally needs the receipt to pass verify_signature and validate_claim and to carry an `attestation` object whose `receipt_key` holds such a value (verified: the only difference between the exit-0 control and the exit-101 run is that one character).

No flags are needed: variant A panics on the first line of the verdict path, variant B on the no---fvk attestation branch. With `--fvk`, the same unchecked short() slices are reached from verify_attestation's mismatch messages (receipt.rs:145-154) for the same class of input (source-verified; not executed here, since it is not the minimum result).

execution.attacker_perspective: Any party whose receipt a verifier inspects - which is the tool's entire purpose - can make `zanary-report verify-receipt` die instead of returning a verdict by putting one non-ASCII character in a hex field. Variant A needs no key and no valid signature; variant B leaves the receipt's signature and claims valid and only attaches an `attestation` object, which the receipt signature does not cover (an attestation can be attached to an already-signed receipt without invalidating it).
payloads: {"label": "verifier-4 probe", "format": "zanary-receipt-v1", "body": "{\"amount_zat\":1234567,\"invoice_id\":\"4471\",\"memo_sha256\":\"60016cf4bf951820ab397c737584734efac9c519a1f8964e8e8d749c62c50748\",\"txid\":\"44f216cc11eb88f67d9976f8ba91f2ac5a981cc8a2f8a648f75887580f57337e\"}", "claims": ["invoice 4471 was paid 1234567 zatoshis in transaction 44f216cc11eb88f67d9976f8ba91f2ac5a981cc8a2f8a648f75887580f57337e"], "discloses": [], "signer": "a€", "signature": "00"}
instructions: Build the reviewed revision in the approved sandbox copy: docker run --rm --network=none --cpus=6 --memory=3500m --memory-swap=5g --pids-limit=1024 -v /home/kiter/.hermes/cache/scratch/zanary-sandbox-w2:/t -v /home/kiter/.cargo/registry:/usr/local/cargo/registry:ro -w /t rust:1-slim sh -c 'CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 cargo build --offline -p zanary-report' (binary sha256 2e903494733440be53a656846c954ccee551f5a740773cf6f585c2b19b534e60).

Write payload 1 (signer "a\u20ac", 4 bytes; signature "00") to /t/v4/payload-a.json and run /t/target/debug/zanary-report verify-receipt /t/v4/payload-a.json; echo exit=$? - expect a panic at crates/report/src/receipt.rs:359:36 and exit 101, with no `signature :` line.

Generate the variant-B fixtures with the target's own signing code: append check-probe-module.txt to the sandbox copy of crates/report/src/receipt.rs (a #[cfg(test)] module; production lines unchanged) and run CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 cargo test --offline -p zanary-report verifier4_probe -- --nocapture --test-threads=1. It writes /t/v4/receipt-b-nonascii.json (signature and claims valid; a wallet attestation attached AFTER signing whose receipt_key is "aaaaaaa\u20acbbbbbbbbbbbbbb", 24 bytes) and its ASCII twin /t/v4/receipt-b-ascii.json.

Run /t/target/debug/zanary-report verify-receipt /t/v4/receipt-b-nonascii.json; echo exit=$? - expect `signature : VALID`, `signer : 280f51c8...55ae602e`, both `claim ok` lines, then a panic at crates/report/src/receipt.rs:190:30 and exit 101.

Controls on the same binary: verify-receipt /t/v4/receipt-b-ascii.json (prints `attested : receipt key 280f51c8... is attested by wallet key 6ebb833c...` and the summary, exit 0) and verify-receipt /t/v4/clean.json (prints `binding : none ...`, exit 0).

Fix check (also run): apply the remediation to the sandbox copy and run CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 cargo test --offline -p zanary-report - 14 unit tests + 4 golden tests pass, variant A becomes the clean error `hex string has a non-hex character (zanary-receipt-v1 says lowercase hex)`, short() returns safely for the variant-B string, and ASCII output is unchanged.
execution.observed_result: Variant A: the `receipt`/`format`/`claim` lines, then `thread 'main' (433) panicked at crates/report/src/receipt.rs:359:36:` / `end byte index 2 is not a char boundary; it is inside '\u20ac' (bytes 1..4 of string)` and exit=101; no `signature :` line was ever printed. Variant B: `signature : VALID (Orchard RedPallas over the receipt's own fields)`, `signer : 280f51c8bafa209126d11a661978c5aa40a4bd61f41eb08fed0fc34255ae602e`, both `claim ok :` lines, then `thread 'main' (440) panicked at crates/report/src/receipt.rs:190:30:` / `end byte index 8 is not a char boundary; it is inside '\u20ac' (bytes 7..10 of string)` and exit=101 - the attestation had been attached after the signature was made and the signature still verified. Unit level: both panics caught under catch_unwind with the same messages and the same file:line:col. Controls on the same build: the ASCII twin of variant B printed `attested : ...` and exited 0; the attestation-free receipt printed `binding : none ...` and exited 0. (stdout is block-buffered into a pipe, so in the transcript the stderr panic text appears ahead of the buffered verdict lines; verbatim runs are in check-cli-repro.txt and check-unit-probe.txt.)

remediation.strategy: Reject non-hex input before any slicing and make the shortening helper char-boundary safe, reusing the implementations the repository already contains (crates/report/src/node.rs:193 and crates/probe/src/bin/zanary-seed.rs:714 decode via hex.as_bytes().chunks(2) + std::str::from_utf8, which returns a clean error instead of panicking). Add both payloads as regression fixtures asserting exit 1 with an INVALID verdict rather than a panic. Verified in the sandbox: with the fix applied, `cargo test --offline -p zanary-report` is 14 passed / 0 failed plus 4/4 golden tests, variant A becomes `Err: ... hex string has a non-hex character (zanary-receipt-v1 says lowercase hex)`, short() returns safely for the variant-B string, and ASCII output stays byte-identical (`short("280f51c8...602e")` still `280f51c8…55ae602e`).

likelihood.reason: The trigger is trivially cheap for anyone who supplies a receipt - one non-ASCII character in `signer` needs no key and no valid signature - but it only fires for a consumer that runs `zanary-report verify-receipt` on that file, which is exactly the tool's documented use (strangers verifying someone else's receipt) and not something the honest producer emits.

impact.reason: Observed effect is a process abort: a Rust panic message plus exit 101, with no verdict and no FAIL line. There is no false PASS (101 is non-zero, so an exit-0 gate is not fooled), no memory corruption and no code execution; the artifact simply cannot be verified by this tool, and the panic message leaks only a source path and the offending string.

confidence.reason: Independently reproduced by this verifier: two CLI panics with exit 101 at the exact file:line:col (receipt.rs:359:36, receipt.rs:190:30) from fixtures generated by the target's own signing code, plus two unit-level panics caught under catch_unwind; the source trace is complete from argv/file read to both sinks, ASCII controls exit 0 on the same binaries, the two safe in-tree variants of the same helper confirm the intended behaviour, and the proposed fix compiles with all existing tests green.
